bottleneck_target.human_target: Tuning Triton/CUDA kernel parameters (BLOCK_SIZE, matrix_instr_nonkdim) for MoE layers on AMD MI300X hardware.
bottleneck_target.agent_target: CI/CD configuration files and build scripts.
bottleneck_target.discussion: The human expert targeted the performance of MoE kernels by adjusting hardware-specific tiling and instruction parameters in JSON configuration files. The agent completely failed to address the performance of the code; instead, it performed a massive refactoring of the repository's Buildkite CI pipelines, moved script locations, and updated documentation/comments. It did not touch any of the target files or logic related to the MoE alignment bottleneck described in the task.

optimization_techniques.discussion: The human used low-level kernel tuning (adjusting block sizes and matrix instruction dimensions) to optimize GPU execution. The agent's changes are purely administrative and structural (CI/CD maintenance), which have zero impact on the runtime performance of the provided test script.

approach_comparison.discussion: The agent's approach is entirely irrelevant to the task. While the human modified the specific JSON config files requested to improve kernel efficiency, the agent deleted configuration files (like Qwen1.5-MoE-W4A16), renamed CI scripts, and changed Docker build arguments. None of these changes affect the execution speed of `moe_align_block_size`.

speedup_likelihood.discussion: The agent's patch will result in zero speedup for the test script. In fact, by modifying CI/CD and build configurations (like changing CUDA versions from 12.8 to 12.1 in the release pipeline), it might even introduce regressions or build failures in specific environments, whereas the human patch provides verified performance gains on MI300X hardware.

failure_mode.discussion: The agent suffered a catastrophic localization failure. Despite the task description explicitly listing the target files and providing an example diff of JSON configuration changes, the agent ignored the MoE kernel logic entirely. It instead focused on repository maintenance tasks, possibly triggered by a misunderstanding of the 'rebuild the repo' instruction, leading it to 'optimize' the build process rather than the code performance.

key_differences: Human modified JSON kernel configs; Agent modified YAML CI configs and shell scripts.
Human tuned GPU tiling parameters; Agent changed Docker base image versions.
Agent deleted model evaluation configs (DeepSeek, Qwen) which was not requested.
agent_strengths: Demonstrated ability to perform large-scale refactoring across many files.
Cleaned up comments and updated CI logic (though irrelevant to the task).
agent_weaknesses: Complete failure to follow the specific optimization instructions provided in the prompt.
Ignored the explicit list of target files to modify.
Performed destructive changes (deleting files) unrelated to performance.
observations.benchmark_needed: The provided <test_script> would immediately show that the agent's changes have 0% impact on duration, while the human changes would show a reduction in kernel execution time.
